slides.text: PRISONERS BUILT THIS PRISON. THEN THEY BURNED IT.
Boise, Idaho. The Old Idaho Penitentiary took its first prisoners in 1872.
Inmates quarried the sandstone and built its walls themselves.
Over 101 years, more than 13,000 people were locked up here, about 215 of them women.
Its most notorious inmate, Harry Orchard, killed a former governor with a bomb. He died inside in 1954.
In 1971 and 1973, inmates rioted over conditions and set buildings on fire.
It closed in December 1973. The burned walls are still standing.
Today it's a museum. Ghost-hunting shows have filmed inside.
